items.followUp: Write the scientific names of wheat and mango.

rubric.why: The scientific name of onion is Allium cepa.
The scientific name of pea is Pisum sativum.

items.followUp: What is synapsis, and during which stage of meiosis does it occur?

rubric.why: Crossing over involves exchange of chromosome material.
rubric.description: Identifies the exchange of segments or genetic material
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromosome segments or genetic material are exchanged.

rubric.why: The exchange occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during prophase I of meiosis.
rubric.description: Identifies the chromatids involved or the stage of meiosis
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, or prophase I of meiosis.

modelAnswer: Crossing over is the exchange of corresponding segments between non-sister chromatids of a pair of homologous chromosomes.
It occurs during prophase I of meiosis and produces new combinations of genes.

items.followUp: What happens to the chromosomes during the S phase of the cell cycle?

rubric.why: S stands for synthesis; DNA is replicated during this phase.
rubric.description: States that DNA is synthesised or replicated
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying DNA synthesis or replication.

rubric.why: DNA replication results in duplicated chromosomes, each consisting of two sister chromatids.
rubric.description: States the result of DNA replication
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromosomes are duplicated or that each duplicated chromosome has two sister chromatids.

modelAnswer: S phase is the synthesis phase of interphase, during which DNA is replicated.
As a result, each chromosome is duplicated and consists of two sister chromatids.

items.followUp: Why is ATP called the energy currency of the cell?

rubric.why: ATP stores energy in its chemical bonds and serves as the cell’s energy currency.
rubric.description: States that ATP stores energy or is the cell’s energy currency
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining ATP’s role in storing or carrying energy.

rubric.why: ATP releases energy to drive cellular activities and reactions.
rubric.description: States that ATP supplies energy for cellular work
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking ATP’s energy to cellular activities or metabolic reactions.

modelAnswer: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the energy currency of the cell because it stores and transfers energy.
When ATP is broken down, it releases energy that cells use for their activities and metabolic reactions.

items.followUp: Write two characteristics of enzymes and give one example of an enzyme.

rubric.why: Enzymes act as biological catalysts and speed up reactions without being used up.
rubric.description: Gives one valid characteristic of enzymes
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a characteristic such as being biological catalysts or speeding reactions without being consumed.

rubric.why: Enzymes are specific in their action; other valid characteristics include that they are proteins and are affected by temperature and pH.
rubric.description: Gives a second valid characteristic of enzymes
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for another distinct correct characteristic.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions without being consumed.
Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.

items.followUp: How do root hairs help a plant absorb water and mineral salts?

rubric.why: Root hairs are fine extensions of cells in the root epidermis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing root hairs as extensions or outgrowths of root epidermal cells.

rubric.why: Root hairs increase the absorbing surface of the root and take up water and mineral salts from the soil.
rubric.description: States the function of root hairs
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining their role in absorption of water and mineral salts, or in increasing the root’s absorbing surface.

modelAnswer: Root hairs are fine, hair-like extensions of the epidermal cells of a root.
They increase the root’s surface area and absorb water and mineral salts from the soil.

items.followUp: How does dietary fibre help prevent constipation?

rubric.why: Dietary fibre adds bulk to the contents of the intestine and to faeces.
rubric.description: States that dietary fibre adds bulk
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that fibre adds bulk to faeces, stool, or intestinal contents.

rubric.why: Fibre helps movement through the intestine and makes faeces easier to pass, helping prevent constipation.
rubric.description: Explains the benefit for bowel movement
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking fibre to easier passage of faeces, bowel movement, or prevention of constipation.

modelAnswer: Dietary fibres, also called roughage, add bulk to the contents of the intestine and to faeces.
They help food and faeces move through the digestive tract and make bowel movements easier, helping to prevent constipation.

items.followUp: Explain how tissues combine to form an organ and how organs combine to form an organ system. Give an example of each.

rubric.why: An organ is made of different tissues working together to perform a particular function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an organ consists of different tissues working together for a function.

rubric.why: An example supports the definition of an organ; valid examples include the stomach, heart, and leaf.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable organ example or its function
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example of an organ, preferably linked to its function.

rubric.why: An organ system is a group of organs that work together to perform a major body function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an organ system consists of organs working together for a function.

rubric.why: Examples include the digestive system, respiratory system, and circulatory system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a valid organ system and, where applicable, one of its organs.

modelAnswer: An organ is a structure made of different tissues working together to perform a particular function.
For example, the stomach is an organ made of tissues that work together in digestion.
An organ system is a group of organs that work together to perform a major function of the body.
For example, the digestive system includes the stomach and other organs that work together to digest food.
